cultural.vision_reason: This is a hand-woven, embroidered cotton robe (boubou/riga style) of the type worn broadly across West Africa, including by Wolof men; the elaborate "aska biyu" hand-embroidery is a widespread regional prestige-garment style plausible for the claimed culture even though the museum's terminology leans Hausa.

physical.title: gown; tobe
physical.summary: Man’s gown (boubou, tobe, riga), hand-woven from hand-spun white cotton. The body is formed of 135 narrow strips hand-sewn together along the selvedges vertically, while the sleeves are sewn horizontally. The body of the gown is rectangular in shape, while the sleeves flare out at the top being wider at the top than at the bottom. At the front is sewn a large pocket. The pocket and gown are hand-embroidered in the ‘two knives’ (aska biyu) pattern using a beige local silk thread (tsamiya or sanyan) and chain and buttonhole eyelet stitching. There is a large spiral shape on the front and another on the back. The neck and sleeves of the garment are hemmed.
